title: Frontend Development Readiness
description: Evaluate your proficiency in HTML5, CSS3, modern JavaScript, React components, state, and browser APIs.

questions.question: Which HTML5 semantic element is most appropriate for containing the primary navigation links of a website?
options: <section>
<nav>
<aside>
<header>
questions.explanation: The <nav> element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links.

questions.question: In the CSS Box Model, which property creates space *inside* the element's border, around the content?
options: margin
padding
outline
gap
questions.explanation: Padding defines space between the content and the inner edge of the border, whereas margin defines space outside the border.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between CSS Grid and CSS Flexbox?
options: Grid is two-dimensional (rows & columns) while Flexbox is one-dimensional (row or column)
Flexbox supports responsive design while Grid does not
Grid only works with HTML5 tables
Flexbox is deprecated in modern browsers
questions.explanation: CSS Grid is a 2D layout system handling rows and columns simultaneously, while Flexbox arranges elements along a single main axis.

questions.question: What will `console.log(typeof null)` output in JavaScript?
options: "null"
"undefined"
"object"
"number"
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, `typeof null` returns 'object' due to a historical legacy bug from the original implementation.

questions.question: What does the JavaScript Event Loop do when a Promise resolves in modern browsers?
options: Places the callback into the Macrotask Queue
Places the callback into the Microtask Queue
Executes the callback synchronously inside the call stack immediately
Spawns a new background operating system thread
questions.explanation: Promise callbacks (.then, .catch, await) are scheduled in the Microtask Queue, which executes before the next Macrotask.

questions.question: In React, what is the key rule when using the `useEffect` hook with an empty dependency array `[]`?
options: It re-runs on every state change
It only runs once when the component mounts
It will never execute
It causes an infinite rendering loop
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array `[]` tells React that the effect doesn't depend on any props or state, so it runs only once after the initial render.

questions.question: Why is the `key` prop essential when rendering dynamic lists in React?
options: It styles list elements automatically
It provides a CSS class identifier
It helps React identify which items have changed, been added, or removed during reconciliation
It acts as a primary key in IndexedDB
questions.explanation: Keys help React's virtual DOM reconciliation algorithm identify individual elements across renders to minimize DOM re-creations.

questions.question: Which HTTP header is primarily used to instruct the browser to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) by restricting resource origins?
options: Content-Security-Policy
Access-Control-Allow-Origin
Strict-Transport-Security
X-Frame-Options
questions.explanation: Content-Security-Policy (CSP) allows site administrators to restrict the resources (such as JavaScript, CSS, Images) that the browser is allowed to load.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of code splitting with dynamic `import()` in frontend applications?
options: Reduces initial bundle size and speeds up initial page load
Encrypts JavaScript source code in production
Eliminates the need for CSS preprocessors
Enables automatic server-side rendering
questions.explanation: Code splitting breaks bundles into smaller chunks loaded on demand, significantly improving First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Time to Interactive (TTI).

questions.question: What is the role of Web Workers in client-side web development?
options: They run background tasks on separate threads without blocking the main UI thread
They cache assets offline in place of Service Workers
They manage CSS animations directly on the GPU
They provide direct access to the DOM from worker threads
questions.explanation: Web Workers allow running CPU-heavy JavaScript scripts in background threads, keeping the browser UI responsive and free from stutter.
